cards.b: The small group of soloists in a concerto grosso (in Handel Op. 6: two violins and a cello).
The larger group (full string orchestra) in a concerto grosso; also called tutti.
Bass line plus chords from harpsichord or organ, played throughout Baroque music.
Main theme for tutti returns between contrasting episodes for the soloist(s).
Sudden changes from loud to soft with no gradual change; typical of the Baroque.
Repeated broken-chord pattern in the left hand; typical of the Classical period.
Dominant in the exposition; tonic in the recapitulation.
An unaccompanied showy passage for the soloist, usually near the end of a concerto movement.
Instrumental music that describes a story, scene or idea, such as Vivaldi's Spring.
Piano, oboe, clarinet, horn and bassoon.
Ternary dance structure: minuet, trio, minuet; in triple time.
A pattern repeated higher or lower in pitch.

cards.f: B flat clarinet: written C sounds...
cards.b: B flat, a major second lower than written.

gaps.s: A small group of soloists in a concerto grosso is called the ___.
The large group of players in a concerto grosso is the ___.
The harpsichord and cello together form the basso ___.
In Baroque music sudden changes of volume are called ___ dynamics.
The main theme that returns in a Baroque concerto is the ___.
In sonata form the themes are explored in the ___ section.
A left-hand pattern of broken chords such as C–G–E–G is an ___ bass.
Vivaldi's Spring is part of The Four ___.

short.q: Give two differences between Baroque and Classical textures.
short.model: Baroque is often polyphonic and imitative with continuo; Classical is mostly homophonic with melody and accompaniment, often an Alberti bass.
The full orchestra plays a main theme (ritornello) that returns in different keys, alternating with solo episodes; the final ritornello is in the home key.
points: keys change / home key at end

short.q: Describe what happens in the development section of sonata form.
short.model: Themes from the exposition are broken up and developed, often by sequence, passing through different keys and building tension.

short.q: Name two ways Vivaldi's Spring is programme music.
short.model: Solo violin trills imitate birdsong; tremolo and fast scales in the minor depict thunder and lightning.

short.q: Why is a chamber work like Mozart's K. 452 different from an orchestral piece?
short.model: It has one player per part and no conductor, so players pass ideas between themselves and the texture is lighter and more varied.
